subject: Chargeflow / NetSuite renewal: recommended path and action items
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Chargeflow / NetSuite renewal: options and timeline

Team —

Quick summary: our current NetSuite subscription (ERP + billing module) renewal window opens mid-November. NetSuite proposed a 12% list increase in their renewal email last month. Separately, our billing usage patterns have shifted (higher metered invoice volume) and the embedded billing product market has matured — Chargeflow and a few others now offer a cheaper per-invoice model that could materially lower unit costs.

As discussed on last week's finance sync, please review two parallel tracks:

1) Renew NetSuite for another 12 months while negotiating a targeted cap and added SLA credits;
2) Build a migration plan to switch to Chargeflow for billing only and keep NetSuite for ERP/GL (hybrid approach).

Asks:
- Laura: procurement to run a pricing leverage analysis and identify our non-negotiables (data export windows, invoicing attachments, tax handling).
- Marissa: run a 6/12/24-month TCO with migration costs (engineering, outage window, and QA).
- Michael: want a thumbs-up on the approach so we can request an extended quote window from NetSuite and start technical scoping for Chargeflow.

Attached: high-level timeline and vendor list (we'll collate vendor bids here).

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: billing-stack-options-2025.pdf (pdf)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Chargeflow / NetSuite renewal: options and timeline

Sounds good — I'm on it. Initial procurement notes:

- NetSuite historically enforces 60-day notice for price lock; we need to secure something by 2025-11-15.
- Negotiation levers: multi-year commit, pre-paid ARR credits, professional services credits, and additional uptime SLAs.
- Must confirm export format for recurring invoices (CSV/API) and whether historical invoice metadata (>24 months) is readily exportable without PS work.

I'll request a formal renewal proposal today and ask for a 45-day lock if we enter an evaluation of a third-party billing provider.

Also looping Alex from Chargeflow (external) if we decide to get an implementation estimate — Alex, if you can provide a one-pager on called-out migration risks and typical timelines that would be helpful.

Best,
Laura
Procurement Manager

Hi Rishi / Laura —

Thanks for the heads up. I've attached our renewal proposal for the 2026 term and a one-page summary showing the line items driving the 12% increase (primarily metered invoice volume and new tax engine fees).

If you are evaluating a third party, I can request a 45-day courtesy hold at my manager's discretion — please confirm by 2025-10-08 so I can escalate.

Key offer highlights:
- 10% discount if you commit to a 2-year renewal and agree to a two-week phased renewal payment schedule.
- 30% credit on PS hours if you sign an enterprise services bundle before renewal.
- Expanded export API access (adds JSON export for invoice history) for an additional one-time fee.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the proposal.

Regards,

NetSuite Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-07T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Chargeflow / NetSuite renewal: options and timeline

Thanks Sarah for the proposal (cc'd above). Quick analysis notes from my side after a first-pass TCO:

Summary: moving billing off NetSuite to a SaaS billing provider (Chargeflow) looks like it could lower annual billing ops cost by ~22% in steady state, but the migration delta (engineering + data migration + validation + 1 quarter of dual-run costs) pushes the 12-month payback to ~18 months. Key callouts:

- Migration risks: invoice attachment mapping, historical tax adjustments, and AR reconciliations. We'll need a 6-week freeze window for invoice runs during cutover (we should avoid EOM close windows).
- Contract levers with Chargeflow: volume-based pricing tiers, indemnity on data exports, and a defined rollback plan for 30 days in case of issues.

I've uploaded a cost sheet and a recommended mutual action plan. Highlights:
- If NetSuite will offer the 2-year 10% discount + PS credits, the net present value difference narrows and I'd recommend taking the renewal while continuing a technical proof-of-concept with Chargeflow (hybrid).
- If NetSuite cannot extend a 45-day lock, pursue Chargeflow fast-track evaluation and request a short-term extension from NetSuite while we run POC.

Attachments: Chargeflow_Pricing_Comparison_2025.xlsx
Link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/finance/billing-stack-eval (MAP and TCO spreadsheet)

-Marissa
Director, Finance Ops

Date: 2025-10-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final recommendation: hybrid path (renew + POC) and ask for exec approval

Michael —

After collecting the proposal and the TCO, my recommendation is: pursue the hybrid path. Specific asks:

1) Approve a 12-week POC budget for Chargeflow (engineering + PS) not to exceed $85k. This covers data mapping, a test cutover run, and two reconciliation cycles.
2) Authorize procurement to accept NetSuite's 2-year 10% discount if they extend a 45-day lock while we run the POC (we would take PS credits if the deal is accepted).
3) Approve contingency fund of $25k for potential dual-run operational costs during the migration quarter.

Rationale in one line: preserves continuity for revenue recognition and GL while allowing a controlled technical evaluation that could lower run-rate billing costs by ~22% in year two.

If approved, Laura will finalize the renewal hold request with NetSuite and Marissa will kick off the Chargeflow POC plan.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
